column12: Judgement: house convention. Cerezyme (imiglucerase) is the therapy GD3 patients are on today and the active comparator in LEAP2MONO, so it is the comparator in the same disease and setting. The case against has three parts. (1) Cerdelga (eliglustat), the same drug class and also an oral Sanofi drug, costs $296,243 per Part D beneficiary in 2024, 6% lower, and an oral GCS inhibitor may be priced off it. It is labelled only for type 1, though. (2) Cerezyme's Part D figure for 2024 is $365,943, and GD3 is dosed at higher weight-based ERT doses than type 1, so a GD3-specific price could be higher. (3) Part B spend is paid at ASP, which already nets out some commercial discounts. No published annual list price for venglustat exists before approval. In EUR because the engine models a company in its reporting currency and converts to dollars only at the end: $316,023.00 at EUR/USD 1.141100 (ECB via fetchers/fx_ecb.py, 2026-09-23) is EUR 276,945.93

column11: Peterschmitt MJ et al., Orphanet J Rare Dis 2019;14:128 (doi:10.1186/s13023-019-1085-6), pooled eliglustat Phase 2 and Phase 3 trials (ENGAGE, ENCORE, EDGE): 74 of 393 patients actively withdrew over 1,400 patient-years of exposure
column12: Judgement on the analogue: eliglustat is the only marketed oral GCS inhibitor, and venglustat is in the same class. A constant hazard of 74/1,400 = 0.0529 per patient-year gives 1 - exp(-0.0529) = 5.15% a year. Case against: trial persistence overstates real-world persistence. In an Israeli single-centre cohort switching from ERT to eliglustat, 12 of 29 stopped, at a median of 4 months, mostly for adverse events (J Clin Med 2022;11:6265, PMC9659144). On the other side, 15 of the 74 trial withdrawals were for pregnancy, which is protocol-driven.

column12: Measured, with no multiple applied. Gross adds each year = the net change plus 5.15% of the prior Cerdelga stock (the discontinuation above). Divided by the prior year's non-Cerdelga pool, that gives 6.1%, 7.4%, 4.1% and 15.3%, a mean of 8.2%. Cerdelga is the incumbent oral GCS inhibitor switched in from ERT, which is the move venglustat asks GD3 patients to make. The case against runs both ways. For higher: venglustat would be the first therapy for GD3's neurological disease, where Cerdelga competed with ERTs that already worked in type 1, and LEAP2MONO showed superiority to ERT on the neurological endpoints. For lower: Cerdelga's own Medicare stock share, 142 of 333 (43%), solves at this discontinuation to only 3.8% a year at steady state. VPRIV is absent from the book's CMS table, so the denominator is incomplete. Cerezyme's Part B and Part D beneficiaries may overlap. All of these are type 1 dominated Medicare patients.
